Hi Diego / Karthik,

Thanks for sending v3 of the Order Form this morning. Procurement had a few quick commercial questions before we send to legal for signature:

- Invoicing entity: procurement requires invoices to be issued to Greenfield Technologies Ltd (their UK entity). Can Redwood invoice a UK entity, or does Redwood require invoices to be issued to the US entity?
- Net terms: our standard is net45 on new vendors. Will Redwood accept net45, or do you need net30 / prepay?
- Withholding: does Redwood accept that Greenfield may be required to withhold tax in limited jurisdictions? If so, can you confirm which entity would be responsible for grossing-up?
- Minimum commit proration: Procurement wants confirmation of how the minimum commit is allocated across quarters if we start mid-quarter.

I attached the latest Order Form (Greenfield_OrderForm_v3.pdf). Can you confirm the above by EOD Tuesday so we can move to Legal?

Best,

Subject: Re: Greenfield Order Form v3 — entity & payment questions

Sara — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Karthik and Monica from Commercial/Billing and Kimberly from Legal for the redline / evidence asks. Answers below and next steps.

1) Invoicing entity: Redwood can invoice via Redwood Inference, Inc. (US) by default. In cases where customers require a local vendor, we can route invoices through our UK entity (Redwood Inference Ltd) but we need tax residency docs and different bank wiring info. If Greenfield needs the UK entity, please confirm the billing address and PO format.

2) Net terms: Our standard for new commercial order forms is net30. We can accommodate net45 for customers with procurement policies on large deals — need Legal approval for SLA/credit exposure. For a GF deal at the committed level, we can accept net45 provided procurement signs a PO and we include a late-fee grace clause in the order form.

3) Withholding: Redwood generally expects customers to bear withholding where required by local law. Redwood does not gross-up automatically. If Greenfield requires Redwood to gross-up, that will be a commercial exception (we should scope the exposure).

4) Minimum commit proration: We normally prorate the first quarter based on the activation date (pro rata by days remaining), then subsequent quarters follow the schedule. If GF wants tranche-based commits, Commercial will draft a schedule.

Next steps:
- Karthik / Monica: please draft the invoice-entity mapping exhibit (who to invoice by country) and a one-paragraph withholding clause we can propose.
- Kimberly: legal redlines on accepting net45 + late-fee language.
- Sara: if you confirm UK invoicing is required, please share Greenfield's tax certificate(s) and the PO template.

I’ll prepare a short summary and a DocuSign-ready order form after we confirm entity.

Thanks,
Diego
Diego Fernandez

Subject: INTERNAL: proposed commercial language for Greenfield (entity + withholding + commit)

Diego / Monica — draft language below we can push to Greenfield. Kimberly, please review for legal comfort.

- Invoice entity mapping (proposed): Redwood Inference, Inc. (US) will be the default invoicing entity. Where Customer requires invoicing to a local Greenfield entity, Redwood may issue invoices from Redwood Inference Ltd (UK) provided Customer supplies tax residency documentation and a valid PO referencing the Redwood SOW. A separate billing exhibit (Exhibit B) will list per-country invoice entities.

- Withholding clause (proposed): Customer is responsible for any withholding taxes required by the taxing authority in the jurisdiction of invoice. If Customer is required by law to withhold amounts, Customer shall provide Redwood with official withholding tax certificates within thirty (30) days. Redwood may request gross-up as a commercial exception in jurisdictions with significant exposure.

- Minimum commit proration: First invoice will be prorated to the activation date on a daily basis. Minimum commit is applied to Customer account and is non-refundable. Any agreed tranche schedule will be appended as a payment schedule in Exhibit C.

I recommend we mark net45 as a procurement concession on the commercial summary; that will require approval from RevOps if exposure > $250k. Monica, can you run the ARR exposure check and confirm?

Thanks — Karthik
